newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling stable against the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling stable against the dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling was stable against the dollar on Tuesday in the absence of strong buying and selling activity, commercial dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) posted a mean shilling rate of 55.75, unchanged from Monday, while on the pound, it was posted at 89.77 from 89.63 on Monday.
Dealers said there was not much movement in dollar/shilling rate due to a lack of interest from importers and exporters.

"The market appears to be at a stalemate with both importers and exporters holding onto their positions. This is likely to remain until it is moved by an abnormal bid or offer," one commercial dealer said.
He added that the shilling seemed stuck at the 55.70/80 level and the market can go either way from there. The current shilling/dollar level appeared a psychological level and was yet to be beaten.
The money market was very liquid with the commercial banks mopping up excess cash from the Treasury Bills auction. Rates slid down to 15 percent from above 25 percent level on Monday.
